correctness.rationale: Every triple 0<=a<b<c is handled. Contracting the sum-c matching gives an interval graph with steps s=c-b and t=c-a and equal cycle rank. The permutation x->x+s mod s+t has gcd(s,t) cycles; removing their final one-per-class vertices leaves a forest. For larger intervals all gcd classes are connected and counting edges gives beta=max(0,N+1-(s+t)+g), hence the displayed formula. Adding successively more than twice the largest old support gives leaf-only matching extensions. The actual checker was replayed at the package path and independently confirmed 13,750 triples, 6,635 extensions and 1,000 random larger cases; these finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural exact prefix-feasibility problem directly motivated by the 2026 forest characterization is solved for the first nontrivial triple support, with a sharp gcd-dependent obstruction and complete independent-cycle count. This distinguishes false positive Sidon-only and crude superlacunarity tests, and supplies explicit extensible binary word prefixes. The invariant is motivated independently of its computation; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or an isolated numerical experiment.
